faq.q: How is my calorie target calculated?
faq.a: We estimate what your body burns at rest from your height, weight and age (the Mifflin-St Jeor formula), multiply it by your activity level to get your TDEE, then adjust for your goal: −500 kcal to lose weight, +500 to build muscle, −200 for body recomposition, and no change to maintain.

faq.q: What do BMI and TDEE mean?
faq.a: BMI (body mass index) compares weight to height; 18.5–24.9 is the standard healthy range, though it ignores muscle and frame. TDEE (total daily energy expenditure) is an estimate of the calories you burn in a day, including activity.

faq.q: Can I rely on the allergy flags?
faq.a: No — treat them as a prompt to check, not a guarantee. We flag dishes whose ingredient names match something you avoid, but we can't see allergen declarations or cross-contamination. Always check packaging and ask the restaurant.
